title.title: Grothendieck's section conjecture over $p$-adic fields
title.subtitle: Claim: for curves of genus $\ge 2$ over $p$-adic fields, every section comes from a unique rational point

beats.text: Rational points of $X$ should be exactly the splittings of its arithmetic fundamental group
Route: build a special cover, lift the section, apply Koenigsmann's birational theorem
Short for its fame: 24 pages plus a 7-page cover construction

achievement.label: Grothendieck's section conjecture (1983), local p-adic case
achievement.context: Before: the birational version (Koenigsmann 2005) and localization of sections (Pop–Stix 2017)
achievement.note: The global corollary covers only curves like $X_0(N)$, $X_1(N)$

smooth proper geometrically connected curve X/k of genus >= 2, the map from X(k) to Delta_X-conjugacy classes of sections of pi_1(X) -> G_k is a bijection

plain: Points on a curve should match exactly the 'splittings' of its symmetry group, like keys to locks

steps: Known: every section points at one spot, a valuation
Build a special cover that rules out the bad spots
Lift the section to a birational one
Koenigsmann's theorem turns it into a real point

voice.text: Rational points should be exactly the splittings of the arithmetic fundamental group.
A special cover lifts each section to a birational one, where Koenigsmann's theorem applies.
Claimed: every section is a point.
